title: Hot spring baths in northern Japan
summary: In Hokkaido's ski resort area he describes the communal hot baths and bathing customs.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Then we were up in Northern Japan.
Yeah. I thought Hokkaido was an island.
Well, it's the northernmost tip of Japan.

Yeah, anyway, we went to northern Japan where there was a ski resort. And where they have this hot water, you could take those baths. And the women would bathe you, you know what I mean, and they would wash you before you got into the big pool. They would wash you, and they'd take a bamboo bucket and rinse you off. And when you got out there

in the cool, you were clean. And you just take your stool and just sit out there and soak, see. You just sit there, maybe ten or 15 minutes, then you get up and they towel you off. And you go and go on about your business.

And men and women used the same privy up there, and nobody paid any attention. It was just a necessity. That's what it was. Ain't nobody made no big bones about it. That was their culture. And we played all through that part of the country up there, then we come back to Tokyo, played up in Takikawa Air Base.
